name: Pediatric Collagenous Gastritis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Pediatric Collagenous Gastritis

criteria.description: Presence of a thickened subepithelial collagen band (>10 micrometers) in gastric mucosa biopsy
Chronic inflammatory infiltrate predominantly composed of lymphocytes and plasma cells in the lamina propria
Chronic or recurrent abdominal pain and anemia in pediatric patient
Exclusion of other causes of gastritis such as Helicobacter pylori infection or eosinophilic gastritis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histological demonstration of thickened subepithelial collagen band with chronic inflammatory infiltrate in gastric biopsy, clinical symptoms consistent with gastritis, and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on histopathological examination of gastric biopsies; clinical presentation is variable but often includes anemia and abdominal pain.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Subepithelial collagen band thickening in gastric mucosa
searchTerms: thick collagen layer in stomach lining

pathognomonic.notes: Due to chronic gastric mucosal bleeding or malabsorption

common.symptomName: Weight loss or failure to thrive

searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells
blood in stool causing dark color
swelling in limbs from low blood protein

laboratory: Iron-deficiency anemia with low serum ferritin
Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: Endoscopic findings may show nodular or erythematous gastric mucosa
No specific radiologic features; imaging mainly to exclude other causes
genetic: No known genetic mutations identified; etiology likely multifactorial
other: Histopathology: thickened subepithelial collagen band (>10 micrometers) with chronic inflammatory infiltrate in gastric biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant eosinophilic infiltration rather than collagen band thickening
Often associated with atopy or allergic history
Presence of Helicobacter pylori on biopsy or urease testing
Associated with villous atrophy in small intestine

redFlags: Rapid progression of anemia despite treatment
Failure to thrive or significant weight loss
references: Kumarasinghe MP, et al. Pediatric collagenous gastritis: a clinicopathologic study. Am J Surg Pathol. 2010.
Feldman M, et al. Sleisenger and Fordtran's Gastrointestinal and Liver Disease, 11th Edition. 2020.
